data.name: Jeronima
data.gender_notes: Jeronima is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Latin, Jeronima means 'liberator of the sacred yoke.' It was a common name for women dedicated to the religious life. The name Jeronima carries the meaning “Liberator of the sacred yoke” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Jeronima usually hope their child will grow to embody liberator of the sacred yoke and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Jeronima belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Liberator of the sacred yoke.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jeronima total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_english.name: Jeronima
in_english.meaning: variant of Jerome, from sacred scripture
in_english.long_meaning: variant of Jerome, meaning devotion and obedience to God's word, derived from Greek Hieronymos, saint of scripture, who translated the Gospel and Paul's epistles into Latin. In Christian tradition, Jerome is revered for his translation of the Bible and his advocacy for a spiritual interpretation of scripture. This name reflects a strong connection to biblical studies and a commitment to faith.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jeronima has its roots in Latin culture and was commonly given to women who were dedicated to religious life. This name is reminiscent of the strong and dedicated women in history who chose to devote their lives to the service of God and the church.
data.spiritual_significance: Jeronima is a name that signifies liberty and dedication. In a spiritual sense, it reminds us of the freedom that comes from being fully committed to one's faith and living a life devoted to God. It also reminds us of the importance of surrendering ourselves to the sacred yoke of God's will and allowing Him to guide us in our lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jeronima: Dedicated to the Virgin Jeronima, a legendary penitent who endured great suffering and became a symbol of deep repentance and devotion to God.

biblical_reference.note: Saint Jerome's writings and translations are referenced in Christian tradition, but the name Jeronima is not a direct biblical reference.

historical_references.reference: Jeronima de Borgonovo, also known as Saint Jerome, was born in 347 AD in Stridon, Dalmatia, in the Roman Empire. He is best known for his translation of the Bible into Latin, known as the Vulgate. His work was influential in the development of the Western Church.

Jeronima de la Fuente, also known as Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz, was born in 1648 in San Juan de los Sabinos, Mexico, in the Spanish colonial era. She is considered one of the greatest writers in the Spanish language, and her poems and plays explored the role of women in society.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Elizabeth Jeronima in Dublin, Ireland credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Jeronima, which means "Liberator of the sacred yoke". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
